description: Phase 1.1 alignment eval: process-behavior cases (machine-checkable against the SKILL.md contract, including review content-blocker gating and two-stage content confirmation) plus a 20-item trigger / near-miss description set for triggering accuracy.

evals.name: new-task-auto-enters-alignment
evals.prompt: I just ran workloom_task_create for 'add offline caching to the mobile client'. The task is in planning and the prd.md is still the skeleton. Take the alignment from here.
evals.expected_output: The skill starts the Phase 1.1 design tree from the Goal/value node, keeps each round to the full current frontier as one numbered batch with a recommendation per decision node, writes settled conclusions into prd.md incrementally, and never asks whether a deep questioning round is wanted.
assertions: opens from Goal and value without asking whether a deep questioning round is needed
lists the whole frontier in one round instead of one question at a time
gives a recommendation with reasoning for each decision node
never loads brainstorm/ui-design fixed question sets

evals.name: ui-applicability-consults-reference
evals.prompt: We are aligning a workloom task that rebuilds the settings screen with a new layout, empty/error states and light/dark theming. Settle the UI applicability node.
evals.expected_output: The alignment marks frontend UI presentation as applicable, reads references/ui-design, walks the seven axes until decidable, and records a ## UI Design section in prd.md.
assertions: loads the UI axes reference (references/ui-design) on the applicability node
covers the seven UI axes or explicitly marks not applicable
records decidable UI requirements in the prd.md ## UI Design section
keeps the UI work as design-tree nodes rather than a separate 1.1b phase

evals.name: test-first-seam-confirmation
evals.prompt: Aligning a workloom task for a payments retry service that clearly needs tests before implementation. Resolve the test-first node and close the loop.
evals.expected_output: The alignment consults references/test-first, asks the applicability question (yes/no/critical paths only), confirms the seams with the user, and writes the confirmed seams into prd.md acceptance criteria.
assertions: asks the test-first applicability question with the three options
consults the test-first reference and confirms the seams before prd.md finalization
records the confirmed seams in acceptance criteria
leaves the red-green method itself to the generic tdd skill in Phase 2.1

evals.name: prd-changed-after-confirm-content-reentry
evals.prompt: The prd.md of an aligned workloom task changed after workloom_task_align confirm (a new platform target appeared) — the user themselves asked for that platform target in their last message. Handle it.
evals.expected_output: The user's own change message is treated as the change confirmation: the skill updates prd.md for the new platform target, re-runs review, and re-runs action=confirm (target=prd) with a fresh summary to refresh the record, then continues — it does not ask the user to confirm the same change a second time, and no hash is involved anywhere.
assertions: updates prd.md for the user-proposed change without asking for confirmation again
re-runs workloom_task_align action=review and then action=confirm with target=prd and a fresh summary
records only the confirmation time and summary (never a hash)
would batch questions to the user instead if the change had been discovered by the agent itself

evals.name: fixed-convergence-order-review-confirm
evals.prompt: The frontier of the active workloom alignment is empty and prd.md is complete with the ## Alignment Decisions section. Take it through convergence.
evals.expected_output: The alignment follows the fixed order: frontier empty → finalize prd → workloom_task_align action=review → require readyToConfirm true (content shown only then) → user explicitly confirms the content → action=confirm with target=prd and a non-empty summary; the record stores only the confirmation time and the summary.
assertions: runs action=review before any confirm
checks readyToConfirm on the review result before involving the user
presents the prd content to the user only once readyToConfirm is true
checks Risks and Open Questions records nothing undecided before confirming (no HTML marker involved)
confirms with target=prd and a summary only after explicit user confirmation, recording no hash

evals.name: review-content-blockers-block-user-confirmation
evals.prompt: The active workloom alignment looks converged, so you run workloom_task_align action=review. The result is readyToConfirm false with structureIssues showing prd.md section "Notes" is missing. Go get the user's confirmation of the snapshot.
evals.expected_output: The review is treated as a hard stop: the missing ## Notes section is a content blocker, so the Agent adds the section (or fills it when the blocker says the section is still a placeholder), re-runs workloom_task_align action=review, and presents the content to the user only once readyToConfirm is true.
assertions: does not ask the user to confirm while readyToConfirm is false
fixes the reported content blocker in prd.md instead of jumping to action=confirm
distinguishes a missing section from a section that is still a placeholder
re-runs action=review after the fix and checks readyToConfirm again
keeps the missing summary out of the content blocker list (it is a confirm call parameter)

evals.name: capability-grouped-narrative-prd-accepted
evals.prompt: A workloom task's prd.md organizes Requirements by capability (R1 caching layer, R2 invalidation policy, R3 offline fallback — each a decidable statement), carries an AC per requirement citing its R numbers with a verification method, and its Alignment Decisions keeps only the three key choices with their rationale. Judge the document against the recording standard.
evals.expected_output: The document passes the narrative bar: the reading main line runs background → goal → scope → requirements → acceptance, requirements are grouped by capability or behavior rather than stacked in Q&A order, every AC traces to an R number with a verification method, and Alignment Decisions keeps key choices with rationale instead of per-round replies.
assertions: accepts the capability-grouped requirements without asking to renumber them by conversation order
checks each AC cites a defined R number and carries a verification method
confirms the Alignment Decisions section holds key choices with rationale, not Q/A numbering
declares the document ready for review without demanding per-round reply transcripts

evals.name: qa-stacked-narrative-prd-flagged
evals.prompt: A workloom task's prd.md lists Requirements as 'R1: from round 1 the user said caching', 'R2: from round 2 the user added invalidation', repeats the same caching summary inside both Requirements and Alignment Decisions, and its Acceptance Criteria say 'AC1: works well' with no R reference and no verification method. Judge the document against the recording standard.
evals.expected_output: The document fails the narrative bar and is sent back for restructuring: Requirements must be regrouped by capability or behavior instead of Q&A rounds, the duplicated caching summary keeps one primary home section and is cross-referenced elsewhere, AC1 must cite a defined R number and carry a verification method, and Alignment Decisions must drop the per-round transcript.
assertions: flags the Q&A-round-stacked requirements as a narrative defect to regroup by capability
flags the duplicated caching summary and keeps one primary home section with cross-references
flags AC1 for citing no R number and carrying no verification method
removes the per-round reply transcript from Alignment Decisions before re-running review

evals.name: plan-pseudocode-standard-pass-and-flag
evals.prompt:
A workloom task is authoring plan.md at 1.4. Step 1's Edit is structured pseudocode: '- Edit:
  Input: locate the retry branch in src/client.js.
  Output: retry returns the normalized payload.
  Preconditions: none
  Procedure: replace the branch body per the anchors.
  Failure: none'. A candidate step 2's Edit only says 'add error handling and update related code'. Judge both against the plan-authoring standard.
evals.expected_output: The structured pseudocode step passes the authoring bar: it anchors to a real file and symbol and carries the five protocol fields in order, with none as the legal value for empty Preconditions and Failure. The vague step is flagged as a defect: no Input/Output fields and no failure-path definition mean the executor would improvise — it returns to authoring with real anchors and the five fields.
assertions: accepts the structured pseudocode step without demanding before/after final code
checks the five protocol fields Input, Output, Preconditions, Procedure, Failure are present and ordered
flags the vague step for missing input/output fields and a missing failure path
treats none as a legal value for an empty Preconditions or Failure field

evals.name: grill-request-inside-workloom-routes-here
evals.prompt: While in an active workloom planning task the user says: 'grill this requirement set before we write plan.md'.
evals.expected_output: The request routes to workloom-alignment: the questioning runs as design-tree rounds with recommendations inside the Phase 1.1 alignment itself.
assertions: treats the request as a design-tree round inside Phase 1.1
keeps the questioning inside the same design-tree alignment instead of opening a separate session
keeps the pressure test inside the same prd.md / Alignment Decisions record
